fields.reasoning: The change set's intent offers two fixes: route a clean round from review to fresh, or let run verdict accept an empty list. Routing is the better fit. The code review workflow (internal/workflow/builtin/review.toml) already gives a critic only to a check with a blocker or major, so a clean round skipping the critic matches existing behaviour. A critic has nothing to judge in an empty round, so starting an agent session for it only spends a session, and an empty verdict list would be a record that says nothing. run verdict's rule that it needs at least one verdict, each naming a finding of the latest round (internal/api/run_review.go), stays a useful guard against a critic that records nothing for a round that has findings. Loosening it would also weaken that guard for the code review critics. plan/fresh and plan/check then judge the clean round as before (review-check passes a round with no confirmed findings), so only the plan workflows' routing changes: a command step or condition between review and critic that sends clean rounds to fresh.
fields.statement: In the plan and plan-milestone workflows, a review round with no findings skips the critic: after plan/review, the run goes to the critic only when the latest round has findings, and a clean round goes straight to plan/fresh. `rhiza run verdict` keeps refusing an empty verdicts list.
